page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.26xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor technology. Driven by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 104 dedicated vCPUs. It is paired with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.85 GB of RAM per virtual core. This configuration establishes a low RAM-to-vCPU ratio tailored specifically for high-density compute tasks.

The server lacks integrated local storage and standalone GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage for system volumes and data persistence. Network connectivity is supported by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, enabling high-throughput data transfer between virtual compute nodes and block storage solutions. The hardware profile prioritizes CPU-intensive execution capacity over local disk input and output performance or graphics acceleration.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6e.26xlarge minimizes overhead spent on unutilized memory capacity or local storage controllers, focusing capital allocation on raw processing core density. Potential tradeoffs include reliance on external network storage for disk operations and a relatively constrained memory footprint per thread. Recommended workload fits include compute-heavy parallel processing, continuous integration build servers, CPU-bound scientific modeling, and distributed ETL batch processes.

The instance features no local storage or discrete GPU hardware, relying on cloud-attached block volumes and a 32 Gbps baseline network interface for external data connectivity. By concentrating hardware resources into high vCPU density rather than large memory buffers or ephemeral storage, ecs.c6e.26xlarge offers a focused profile for compute-bound operations. Primary operational tradeoffs stem from its modest per-core RAM allocation and total dependency on network-attached storage. This hardware configuration is suited for batch processing, software compilation, parallel simulation workloads, and CPU-driven data transformations.
